---
title: "Nova and Inventory Start bridge qualification"
description: "App-specific action boundaries, route registries and offline parity required before native cutover."
---

Nova and Inventory use the shared
[Start bridge](/build/devops/start-bridge) for request context, Next adapters,
function guards, route dispatch, cookies and base paths. App code must not copy
those implementations. The canonical codemod supplies the RSC page adapter, router and Worker entry.
Source registration alone does not establish an accepted native build, staging
behavior or production cutover. Retained action imports use the shared React
server-action transport in the native build.

## Route registration

Both apps declare `start-bridge.routes.json`. Regenerate and check from the root:

```sh
node scripts/start-bridge-codemod/cli.mjs nova --apply
node scripts/start-bridge-codemod/cli.mjs inventory --apply
bun packages/start-bridge/src/codegen/cli.ts check apps/nova apps/inventory
```

Registries live under each app's `src/start-bridge/`. Nova includes both OG
`route.tsx` handlers, not only its `route.ts` files. Nova declares the existing portable
`@cloudflare/pages-plugin-vercel-og` renderer. The generated preset resolves `next/og`
to its API; do not remove routes to satisfy the registry.
Changes to public assets must also refresh `public-assets.bridge.gen.ts` before
sealing. Generated manifests prove source coverage, not page or API behavior.

The generated Worker entries use the shared `createBridgeHandler` and read the
matcher from each app's proxy configuration. Inventory excludes `_next` and
dotted paths.
Its existing proxy retains public storefront/webhook exceptions, workspace
session requirements and inventory-specific rate limits. The bridge resolves ownership per request; current app options admit only the
declared root hosts. Inventory keeps Web-owned paths ahead of
local endpoints using the existing Next configuration's reserved API paths. Server functions compile at `/_serverFn`; the shared fetch helper
and Worker apply the resolved mount. Cookies remain unchanged and shared, as
defined by the owning bridge/auth contract. Login pages derive native callback
URLs from the active request context and base, while retained Next requests use
the configured app URL. Inventory builds local login and locale redirects from
`request.nextUrl.clone()` so the Next base path and query survive. The login-mount
and proxy regressions cover both root and apex callbacks; central Web login
return-app classification must also recognize mounted callbacks before acceptance.

The exact `GET` and `HEAD` `/api/build-info` endpoint is public deployment
metadata. Both app proxies follow CMS: remove ambient cookies and authorization,
skip app-session refresh for that read, and retain the API guard. Mutation
methods and path lookalikes keep their existing session and guard boundaries.
The app-owned `proxy-build-info.test.ts` suites cover these boundaries; the
generated emitted-runtime assertion must still verify the compiled source SHA
through an anonymous request.

## Root hosts and response policy

Both native apps are root-only while apex cutover is held. Their app-owned
`start-bridge.config.ts` sets `mountHosts: []` and `unknownHost: 'reject'`:

| App | Production root | Staging root |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nova | `nova.tuturuuu.com` | `nova-staging.tuturuuu.com` |
| Inventory | `inventory.tuturuuu.com` | `inventory-staging.tuturuuu.com` |

Apex paths, suffix lookalikes and unlisted hosts, including Workers preview
hosts, return the bridge's 404 before app dispatch. The generated runtime gate
uses raw Host headers to test each allowed root and the rejected hosts.
Inventory declares its anonymous root outcome as 307; Nova declares 200.

Every response receives the app's robots policy, anti-framing CSP,
`X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and
`Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. The CSP retains the existing
Next `frame-ancestors 'none'` policy from `packages/utils/src/next-config.ts`.
A stricter script policy also requires nonce support for app-owned and library
inline scripts; verify that compatibility in the real browser before adopting it.

Robots decisions read `APP_SEO_POLICY`, not a deployment environment switch.
Nova preserves its policy's public learning and competition pages on the
production host, including supported locale prefixes. Other Nova paths and all
staging responses are private. Inventory's current policy has no indexed
paths, including its Storefront-facing APIs. Storefront's separate SEO policy
continues to own its customer pages.

Every non-asset response forces `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, replacing
upstream max-age directives, and varies on Cookie while retaining other Vary
values. Only GET/HEAD requests under `/assets/` or for exact generated public
files preserve asset caching. A file-like API path or a mutation method does
not receive that exemption. Unit tests cover upstream max-age overrides and
method/path negatives; each app's `response-policy.runtime.mjs` checks the real
emitted Worker on production, staging and rejected hosts. Browser acceptance
also verifies CSP-compatible hydration and navigation.

The app-owned config keeps its top-level imports compatible with Node type
stripping for the generated mount probe. The response decorator loads its
app-owned policy module when it handles a response. The compatibility CLI
`scripts/ci/nova-inventory-native-artifact.py` delegates to the generated
per-app artifact helper, so compatibility flags and public-file identity have
one canonical owner.

## Nova server actions

The generated page adapter sends existing React `use server` calls through the
shared Start server-action transport. Keep the original action imports and
server implementations; do not maintain a second app-specific transport or move
admin-client imports into a client entry.

| Existing action | Transport method | Required supplier behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addWhitelistEmail` | POST | Enabled global role manager; permission is checked before insert. |
| `fetchAdmins` | POST | Authenticated actor with an enabled management role. |
| `fetchSessionDetails` | POST | Session belongs to the request actor and requested challenge. |
| `fetchAllProblems` | POST | Own challenge session, or an enabled manager of that challenge for another user or a sessionless read. |
| `getFullSubmission` | POST | Bound session owner or challenge manager; hidden cases require that manager. |
| `sendOtpAction`, `verifyOtpAction` | POST | Existing central-auth-only rejection; no local OTP flow. |

The shared function proxy refreshes/guards transport; it does not replace these
domain checks. Layout authorization is also insufficient for a direct callable.
The action-security tests cover the original suppliers. Shared bridge tests cover
reply encoding and dispatch; emitted RPC and browser execution require native
acceptance.

## Inventory offline behavior

Existing workspace actions use the shared server-action transport with the
current request's forwarded auth. The offline mutation route remains the existing
thin adapter to `@tuturuuu/inventory-core/offline-create-route`.

Inventory deliberately has no browser service worker. Preserve its
`OfflineProvider register={false}` and missing-worker regression. The shared
offline package's default root-scoped registration must not become active as a
side effect of moving layouts. Do not invent a worker route, register a root
worker on the apex, or clear another app's registrations to pass acceptance.

`offline-handler.test.ts` exercises the real route adapter through the shared
Worker handler at root and `/inventory`: original operation/workspace forwarding,
201/200 receipt status, contract header, terminal 503, missing worker and method
denial. Proxy and domain boundaries use fixtures. Retain the inventory-core
permission/replay tests, offline/stale checkout denial and actor/workspace-scoped
season-merge recovery tests. See
[Inventory browser offline behavior](/platform/applications/inventory#browser-offline-behavior).

## Qualification and cutover

Run unit/types on Sonha and heavy build/runtime/browser work on Thanh through
the shared resource queue. Frozen installs can make workspace bin files
executable; require a clean source check and reconcile such a mode change with
the owning package rather than silently accepting a different source tree.

When transferring built workspace dependencies between runners, bind them to
the exact source and lockfile, verify the archive hash and allowlist its paths
before extraction. On macOS, create these archives with `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1`
so AppleDouble metadata does not add siblings outside the declared `dist`
directories. Regenerate a rejected archive; keep the extraction whitelist intact.

For each exact candidate head require applicable lint/types/unit checks, real
`vp build`, source-bound sealed output, emitted Worker acceptance and browser
acceptance at root and the app mount. Exercise anonymous/signed/wrong-app sessions,
refresh and logout, native RPC, central forwarding and private/public route
boundaries. Inventory additionally verifies that no service-worker registration
is attempted, checkout is blocked offline, and unresolved recovery retains the
same operation identity after reload. Nova verifies both OG image responses and
manager/participant/foreign-user action controls. At the apex, assert the actual
central-login destination and nested callback, not just a redirect status: Web
and the mounted app share an origin, while their login paths remain distinct.
A bare `/verify-token` request intentionally redirects when its token is missing;
it is not an anonymous HTML or offline-provider probe.

After the native build, use `scripts/ci/nova-inventory-native-artifact.py` with
`nova` or `inventory` as its first argument. It reuses the reviewed Apps artifact
contract with the selected app's staging Worker identity and every checked-out
public asset. Set `START_BRIDGE_SOURCE_SHA` to the exact built commit. The
remaining arguments are the shared helper's `seal`, `verify`, `pack` and
`restore` commands; provide runner-owned receipt/archive paths. Restore requires
a fresh output tree with the same checked-out public sources. Verify the seal
again after runtime/browser checks. The helper performs no publication.

`python3 scripts/ci/nova-inventory-native-artifact.test.py` checks sealing,
restoration, identity refusal and tamper detection using synthetic output. Those
fixtures do not qualify an emitted Worker or replace runtime/browser checks.
When running the shared artifact source tests on macOS, use a canonical
`TMPDIR` (for example `/private/tmp`): the race-injection fixture compares the
move destination with its temporary path, while the implementation resolves that
path. A `/var` to `/private/var` alias prevents the fixture from injecting its
symlink; it is not evidence that the negative control ran.

An M4 storage refusal moves `check:changed` to a verified Thanh bundle; it does
not authorize a disk override. Independent security review and an explicit
cutover PR remain required. No migrations or production publication are part of
the preparatory ports.
